q: What does the data quality rating (DQR) on a PEF or EPD mean?
title: Data quality rating (DQR) explained
short: The DQR is a score for how well the data behind a footprint fits the product. Under the EU PEF method it is the average of four ratings, technological, geographical and time representativeness and precision, each from 1 (best) to 5 (worst). Lower is better, and the category rules for your product set the maximum score they accept.
audience: Exporters to the EU receiving PEF-style data requests

p: Commission Recommendation (EU) 2021/2279 sets DQR = (TeR + GeR + TiR + P) / 4. Each criterion gets a rating from 1 to 5 for a dataset. The result maps to quality levels from excellent to poor, and the PEF category rules (PEFCR) for a product set the maximum DQR allowed for each kind of data. Check the PEFCR your buyer uses.

ul: TeR, technological: does the data describe your actual process and machines, or a generic one?
GeR, geographical: is it from your country and grid, or another region?
TiR, time: how close is the data year to the reference year of the study?
P, precision: was it measured or calculated from records, or estimated?

sections.h: How an Indian supplier improves its score
ol: Use your own metered kWh and fuel invoices for the year studied: better TiR and P.
Use the Indian grid factor, such as the CEA CO2 Baseline Database, not a European average: better GeR.
Describe your real process route, for example induction furnace or coal-fired boiler: better TeR.
Ask key suppliers for their own data instead of database averages.

sections.h: PEF and EPD are not the same scale
p: The four-part DQR formula is a PEF rule. An EPD under EN 15804+A2 carries its own data quality assessment, and other programmes use their own scales. Read which method a buyer means before comparing scores.

example.title: Worked example: one dataset, before and after
lines: Before: TeR 2, GeR 3 (European grid average), TiR 1, P 2
After switching to the Indian grid factor: GeR 1
DQR = (2 + 1 + 1 + 2) / 4 = 1.5, a better score from one change
